titulo: An action with consequences needs a human: confirmation and consequentialHint
lead: Booking, canceling, paying, deleting. The agent may pick the wrong tool, misread the description, or obey planted text. The WebMCP spec answers with consequentialHint, so the client can require confirmation. In this lesson you add the annotation and your site's own confirmation, and you prove that declining changes nothing.
objetivo: add consequentialHint and a confirmation with target and effect to every tool that changes something, and prove that declining changes nothing.

aprende.t: Misdescribed intent: the spec's finalizeCart case
consequentialHint (a signal for the client) and the site's confirmation (your lock)
The test that declines and checks that nothing changed
The limit: an agent that operates the screen can click the button too

hero_alt: Confirmation dialog on a dark screen with two neutral buttons, a person's hand near the mouse, neutral light.

secoes.titulo: From request to effect, with a person in the middle

nos.detalhe: The agent calls cancelar_agendamento with {"codigo":"AG-1"}. It may be what the user wanted, or text planted in a review.
consequentialHint: true tells the client the action is significant, real, or irreversible. The spec (§6.4.5) says the client may then require confirmation. May, not must.
Your page shows the question with the target and the effect spelled out: "Cancelar o agendamento AG-1 (m-102, Rita)? A vaga volta para a agenda." And it waits.
Confirm runs it. Decline returns {cancelado:false} and changes nothing. Aborting the run (the signal) counts as a decline.

secoes.legenda: The annotation is for the client; the confirmation is yours. One doesn't replace the other.

texto: The question says what, whose, and what happens next. "Are you sure?" won't do: the person doesn't know what they're approving.
One question per call, with that call's arguments. If the target changes, it's a new question. Never a "yes" that covers the next ones.

passos.titulo: A name that states the effect
texto: The spec shows finalizeCart: the agent thought it was only closing the cart to look, and the tool made the purchase (§6.3.2.3). Name and description state the effect: comprar_carrinho, "charges the saved card".

The dialog lives on the page, and an agent that operates the screen can click Confirm too. checar.mjs itself clicks, the way an agent would. For a high-value action, ask for something the agent doesn't have: the password again, or a code sent to the person.

secoes.titulo: The second hole: canceling without asking
secoes.sub: Edit cancelar_agendamento in kit/pagina/ferramentas.mjs as in the snippet and run the checker. The finished version is in kit/solucao/aula3/.

secoes.sub: The lock, in the kit and on your page.

exercicios.texto: Put consequentialHint and the confirmation in cancelar_agendamento and run the check afterward block.
In agendar_mentoria, replace const ok = await ui.pedirConfirmacao(…) with const ok = true and run the checker. Then undo it.
exercicios.pronto: FALHA agendar_mentoria: agiu sem pedir confirmação and saída: 1; once undone, RESULTADO: 0 falhas.

exercicios.texto: List the tools on your site that change something. Each one gets consequentialHint: true and a question that names the target and the effect.
exercicios.pronto: grep -c "consequentialHint: true" [your tools file] → the number of tools on your list.

perguntas.p: What does the spec say the client can do when it sees consequentialHint?
opcoes: Require user confirmation before running it
Run it without asking, because the site already confirms
Refuse the tool for all users of the site
Swap the tool for the read-only version
perguntas.explica: §6.4.5: the signal lets the client require confirmation selectively. It is something the client may do, so the site needs its own confirmation.

opcoes: "Are you sure you want to continue with this action right now?"
"Confirm?" with the button already selected to speed things up
"Cancel booking AG-1 (m-102, Rita)? The slot goes back to the calendar."
"Do you want to allow all actions from this agent, on this and future visits to the site?"
perguntas.explica: Target and effect spelled out, one question per call. The others ask for a yes without saying what for, or a yes that covers many actions.

perguntas.p: Why does the course say confirmation on the page has a limit?
opcoes: Because the polyfill does not show dialogs on the page
Because an agent that operates the screen also clicks Confirm
Because the spec forbids dialogs inside the tool's execute
Because the signal closes the dialog before the person reads it
perguntas.explica: checar.mjs clicks the button, as an agent would. For a high-value action, ask for something the agent does not have.

perguntas.p: In the spec's finalizeCart case, what went wrong?
opcoes: The agent did not have permission to use the tool
The tool asked the agent for too much personal data during checkout
The iframe from another origin called the tool on its own
The name and description hid the fact that the tool made a purchase
perguntas.explica: Misrepresented intent (§6.3.2): the agent read "finalizes the cart" as "shows the cart". The name and description must state the effect.

itens.texto: consequentialHint on every tool that changes something.
From the site, with target and effect, one per call; refusing changes nothing.
A button on screen is one the agent also clicks; high value calls for what only the person has.
